data.title: Citigroup Cuts Bitcoin and Ethereum Base-Case Targets to $99,532 and $2,838
data.description: According to ChainCatcher citing The Block, Citigroup lowered its base-case price targets for Bitcoin to $99,532 and Ethereum to $2,838 after a further decline in crypto markets. Citi strategist Alex Saunders attributed the cuts to weaker ETF demand, deleveraging in futures markets, a stronger U.S. dollar, rising real yields, and increased stock-market volatility.

data.title: Copper Rebounds From Steep Drop as Physical Tightness Persists
data.description: According to Bloomberg, copper partially recovered after a steep drop on Wednesday, with physical tightness persisting as traders weighed whether a sharp unwinding of bullish bets tied to artificial intelligence and US tariffs had gone too far.

data.title: Grayscale Says Bitcoin Volatility Matches U.S. Large-Cap Stocks, Small Allocation Can Improve Portfolio Efficiency
data.description:
According to ChainCatcher, Grayscale said Bitcoin’s realized volatility has declined significantly over the past decade to about 43%, within the range for U.S. large-cap stocks and below that of roughly 19% of S&P 500 constituents.

Bitcoin has experienced extreme moves in both directions, with momentum concentrating returns and sharp reversals. Its annualized return over the past three years was 60%; excluding its 10 best days would reduce that to 7%, while excluding its 10 worst days would raise it to 197%. Adjusted for volatility, its drawdowns are less extreme than their absolute size suggests. Traditional market factors explain less of Bitcoin’s returns than they do for stocks, bonds and private assets, supporting its role as a portfolio diversifier.

Historical backtests indicate that a small Bitcoin allocation can improve portfolio efficiency without a proportional increase in volatility or maximum drawdown. Bitcoin accounts for about half of return variation in the crypto sector, whose correlations have declined from their peaks as leadership rotates among assets. Grayscale said crypto risk frameworks should reflect the asset class as it exists today, rather than a decade ago.

data.title: Intel’s 18A Process Signs Its First External Customer
data.description:
According to Jin10, Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan said on Wednesday that the company had signed its first external customer for its 18A chip manufacturing process. Speaking at the TomorrowX Summit in Austin, Tan said, “I am personally involved in 18A production, and we have just signed our first customer.” He did not identify the customer.

Intel has viewed the 18A process as key to turning around its business after years of setbacks and low chip yields, as it seeks to become a competitive chip manufacturer for external customers. Intel CTO Ranade later said on social media that the customer had signed up to use Intel’s 18A-P process node, which entered risk production in June.

A report in May said Apple and Intel were nearing an agreement for Intel Foundry Services to produce some chips for Apple devices. Creative Strategies analyst Ben Bajarin said potential customers include Nvidia, Apple, and large hyperscale cloud service providers that design their own custom processors.

data.description: According to Jin10, Bank of Japan Governor Kazuo Ueda said AI demand, the situation in the Middle East and foreign exchange markets need to be monitored.

data.title: Barclays, Deutsche Bank See Dollar Rally Extending Through 2027
data.description: According to ChainCatcher citing Bloomberg, at least three banks expect the dollar’s rally to continue through 2027, despite concerns that slower AI spending could weaken the currency. The AI boom has prompted global investors to buy U.S. stocks, supporting dollar demand as overseas investors exchange their local currencies to purchase shares in American companies using the technology. Barclays says the U.S. private sector is entering a four-year AI investment cycle. It sees strong U.S. economic performance and the possibility of interest rates staying elevated for longer as favorable conditions for the dollar. The report also discusses Barclays’ and Deutsche Bank’s views on the AI boom and the dollar.

data.description: According to ChainCatcher, U.S. President Donald Trump described Nvidia founder and CEO Jensen Huang as an exceptional talent and said he could not be replaced.

data.description: According to Bloomberg, China began marketing dollar-denominated sovereign bonds in Hong Kong, seeking to raise as much as $2 billion in its second offshore note offering this month.

data.title: Blue Owl Readies $513 Million CMBS for Amazon-Leased Data Center Acquisition
data.description: According to Bloomberg, Blue Owl Capital Inc. is preparing to sell $513 million of commercial mortgage-backed securities to fund the acquisition of a Northern Virginia data center fully leased to Amazon.com Inc., people with knowledge of the matter said.

data.title: Ethereum Foundation Sells 1,200 ETH Worth About $2.14 Million
data.description: The Ethereum Foundation exchanged 1,200 ETH, worth about $2.14 million, through CoWSwap for USDS and sUSDS. According to Odaily, it deposited 1.777 million USDS into Sky’s savings contract and received 1.591 million sUSDS. After the transaction, the foundation held 30.78 million sUSDS, worth about $34.47 million, which can earn returns through Sky’s floating savings rate.

data.description: According to Jin10, the Australian dollar fell to its lowest level against the U.S. dollar since January 2026 after Australian unemployment data was released.

data.title: STOCKS | Morgan Stanley Cuts Tencent Price Target Nearly 13% to HK$480, Maintains Overweight Rating
data.description:
According to Sina Finance, Morgan Stanley cut its target price for Tencent by nearly 13% to HK$480 while maintaining an Overweight rating, saying increased AI investment would pressure the company’s near-term earnings. Analysts including Gary Yu said management believes the restrictions have limited impact on cloud revenue, efficient inference can run on domestically made chips, and WorkBuddy can obtain a diversified supply of tokens from model partners.

Weak consumption, the mini-drama business and earlier memory-price increases are expected to constrain core business margins over the next several quarters. Tencent’s core business remains among the strongest in China’s internet industry. While increased AI investment will weigh on near-term earnings, AI productivity products and Xiaowei have considerable long-term potential.

data.title: AI TRENDS | OpenAI’s First AI Hardware Device May Begin Shipping by Year-End
data.description: OpenAI may begin shipping its first AI hardware device by the end of this year. According to Odaily, multiple Chinese manufacturers are involved in the project. Earlier reports said the consumer device, developed with a team led by former Apple Chief Design Officer Jony Ive, would be a screenless, doughnut-shaped device with a microphone, speaker, camera and other sensors. It would primarily interact with users through voice and be able to perceive its surroundings, though specific product details have not been confirmed.

data.title: China Crude Imports Recover as Beijing Restarts Stockpiling
data.description: According to Bloomberg, China’s crude appetite is recovering faster than expected in the final months of 2026. Lower oil prices are prompting cash-strapped refiners to use government-granted import allowances and rebuild stockpiles depleted by months of war.

data.title: Microsoft Says Global Outage Was Unrelated to AI; X User Calls Password Story a Joke
data.description:
According to Sina Finance, Microsoft said its November 12 global outage was unrelated to cybersecurity, AI or AI agents, while X user @nik0p0l5 said a viral post claiming AI could not find a root password was a joke. The outage affected services including Outlook and Exchange for about 24 hours on November 12 and 13, impacting millions of accounts. On November 14, the user said the post was a prank; Microsoft executive Charles Lamanna also said the outage was neither a cyberattack nor caused by AI tools.

Microsoft’s preliminary report, released November 15, said a software defect, a surge in network traffic and reduced server capacity combined to cause the outage. A July code update to Microsoft 365 network gateway servers contained a latent flaw that triggered lock contention in a Windows process under certain workloads, consuming CPU and memory and leaving servers unresponsive. Differences between stress-test traffic and hardware configurations and those in production meant the flaw went undetected for more than three months.

The day before the outage, a separate incident put about 14% of Microsoft’s internal server capacity out of service. About 15 hours before the outage, Teams switched from a backup gateway to a primary gateway that also carried services including Exchange Online, sharply increasing traffic and changing its mix. As servers stopped responding, traffic shifted to other servers and added to their load; safeguards failed to contain the spread, which reached network gateway infrastructure worldwide. Microsoft said it would issue a final post-incident report this week and expected to provide a comprehensive list of remediation projects on November 20.

data.title: Tether Cites 'The Big Short' in Response to S&P's USDT Reserve Risk Assessment
data.description:
According to ChainCatcher citing S&P Global Ratings, S&P kept USDT at the lowest tier of its stablecoin stability assessment, a score of 5 (weak), unchanged from its November 2025 review. S&P data showed that higher-risk assets—including gold, Bitcoin, listed stocks, secured loans and corporate bonds—equaled 28% of USDT in circulation as of September 30, 2026, up from 24% a year earlier.

Tether said the issue lay with S&P's assessment framework, not its reserves, and cited the film “The Big Short” in its response. Tether's reserve report as of September 30 showed about $191.5 billion in assets against $183.5 billion in liabilities, leaving approximately $7.95 billion in excess assets. S&P said it did not lower the score further because it was already at the lowest level.

data.title: Whale Holds About $96.34 Million in Anthropic-Related Shorts on Hyperliquid, Up $4.05 Million
data.description: A whale holds about $96.34 million in Anthropic-related short positions on Hyperliquid. According to Odaily, Onchain Lens detected the positions across two wallets, involving ANTH and ANT pre-market contracts. The positions have about $54.93 million in margin and roughly $4.05 million in unrealized profit; the wallets’ combined historical profit and loss is about $5.75 million.

data.title: Mystery Company Says It Bought More Than $2 Million in TRUMP Tokens for Third Trump Crypto Dinner
data.description: An unidentified digital finance company says it bought more than $2 million worth of TRUMP tokens over the past two months to compete for a seat at the upcoming third Trump cryptocurrency dinner. According to Odaily, the company has not disclosed its identity or the source of the funds, and the dinner is scheduled for November 22 at a Trump golf club outside Washington. The token-holder dinner has drawn conflict-of-interest concerns. U.S. Democratic Senator Elizabeth Warren said she would make the Trump family’s cryptocurrency business a focus of oversight investigations.
